cards.name: Corner Pin
cards.summary: Moves the four corners of a layer independently, so a flat image is skewed into perspective. The standard tool for putting footage onto a screen, sign or document in the shot.
use_for: replace a TV / phone / billboard screen with a news clip
lay a document or newspaper scan onto a desk plate
tilt a quote card or photo into perspective for an explainer
fake a 3D panel flying in on a reel
avoid: crossing two pins makes a bow-tie fold that looks broken
a static pin on a moving shot slides; track it (Mocha / Track Motion > Perspective Corner Pin)
extreme pins soften the image; start from a high-res source

params.name: Upper Left
params.does: position of the top-left corner (layer pixels)
params.typical: [0, 0] default; pull inward 100-300 px for a tilt

params.name: Upper Right
params.does: position of the top-right corner

params.name: Lower Left
params.does: position of the bottom-left corner

params.name: Lower Right
params.does: position of the bottom-right corner

cards.scripting: Points are in the LAYER's own pixel space, not comp space; for a 1920x1080 layer they match the comp. Keyframe all four corners together. The layer bounds grow to the pinned shape, so anything outside the quad is transparent.

verified.note: The whole photo is pinned into a tilted quad with black (transparent) margins, a clear perspective skew.

cards.name: Detail-preserving Upscale
cards.summary: Enlarges a layer while keeping edges sharper than a plain transform scale. Meant for blowing up low-res stills and archival footage to fill the frame.
use_for: fill a 1920 frame with a 640/720p archival clip or a low-res press photo
clean punch-in on an interview without the blur of Scale > 100%
upscale a screenshot for an explainer zoom
avoid: high Detail on compressed (WhatsApp / YouTube) sources exaggerates block artefacts
slow on long clips; pre-render or upscale once
do not also scale the layer transform above 100% (double softening)

params.name: Scale
params.does: enlargement in percent of the source size

params.name: Detail
params.does: how much edge detail is reconstructed / sharpened

params.name: Reduce Noise
params.does: smooths noise before enlarging

params.name: Alpha
params.does: method used for the alpha channel (2-item popup)

cards.equivalent: Motion > Scale (no detail-preserving effect in Premiere)
cards.scripting: Designed for a small source layer scaled to comp size; the two unnamed header items are the 'Fit to Comp Width/Height' buttons and cannot be set from a spec. Scale enlarges the layer's own pixels (bounds grow), so on a full 1920x1080 layer Scale 200 shows as a 2x crop-in. Alpha popup: 1 Detail-preserving, 2 Bicubic (the default) (read from After Effects 26.0); leave it at default.

verified.note: Scale 200 on the full-size layer shows as a 2x crop-in on the frame centre, soft but clean, as the scripting note says.

cards.name: Displacement Map
cards.summary: Pushes pixels horizontally and vertically according to the colour or brightness of a map layer. Used for heat-haze, liquid, glitch and 'image wraps onto a surface' looks.
use_for: glitch transition driven by a noise / blocky precomp
heat-haze or water wobble over a shot
wrap a flag or logo onto cloth / texture
subtle shimmer on a trailer title
avoid: large values with a sharp map tear the image into stair-steps
forgetting Wrap Pixels Around leaves transparent edges
a map layer left visible on top shows in the render (turn its video off)

params.name: Displacement Map Layer
params.does: layer whose pixels drive the displacement (defaults to the layer itself)
params.typical: a hidden Fractal Noise / Turbulent Noise precomp

params.name: Use For Horizontal Displacement
params.does: map channel used for X shift

params.name: Max Horizontal Displacement
params.does: maximum X shift in pixels (sign flips direction)

params.name: Use For Vertical Displacement
params.does: map channel used for Y shift

params.name: Max Vertical Displacement
params.does: maximum Y shift in pixels

params.name: Displacement Map Behavior
params.does: how a map of a different size is placed

params.name: Edge Behavior
params.does: Wrap Pixels Around checkbox

params.name: Expand Output
params.does: checkbox: lets displaced pixels spread past the layer bounds
params.typical: 1 default; 0 to keep the result inside the frame

cards.equivalent: Turbulent Displace (closest; Premiere has no map-layer displacement)
cards.scripting: 'Displacement Map Layer' is a layer reference: set it by layer index in the script, not via demo_settings. It defaults to the layer itself, so the demo values warp the shot by its own luminance. The map is read from the map layer's SOURCE (before its effects/masks); precompose the map to include its effects. Max displacement values are pixels and may be negative. Map value 50% grey = no shift; black pushes the full negative amount, white the full positive amount, so a map with no mid-grey shifts the whole image.

verified.note: The shot is warped by its own luminance into a liquid, smeared distortion (stripes, faces and foreground blocks wobble and tear).

cards.name: Liquify
cards.summary: Brush-based push, twirl, pucker and bloat distortion painted by hand in the Composition panel. Nothing changes until strokes are painted into its distortion mesh.
use_for: caricature / meme distortion on a satire reel (non-news)
melt or smear transition on an abstract element
small cosmetic fixes on product or object shots
avoid: never reshape a real politician's or person's face in news / documentary work: reads as manipulated media
strokes cannot be authored by script, so it cannot be fully automated
large distortions smear texture and look cheap

params.name: Distortion Percentage
params.does: scales the painted distortion (0 = none, 100 = as painted)
params.typical: keyframe 0 -> 100 to reveal a painted warp

params.name: Brush Size
params.does: brush radius for painting strokes (UI only)

params.name: Brush Pressure
params.does: brush strength for painting strokes (UI only)

params.name: Turbulent Jitter
params.does: randomness of the Turbulence tool

params.name: Reconstruction Mode
params.does: how the Reconstruction tool restores the mesh

params.name: Freeze Area Mask
params.does: mask whose area is protected from distortion

cards.scripting: The distortion lives in 'Distortion Mesh' (custom type), which a script cannot create; only a manually painted Liquify can be animated afterwards via 'Distortion Percentage' or 'Distortion Mesh Offset'. Brush/tool settings do not render on their own. For automated warps use Turbulent Displace, Bulge or Twirl instead.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (the distortion mesh must be painted by hand), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Magnify
cards.summary: Shows an enlarged circle or square of the image, like a magnifying glass, over the rest of the frame.
use_for: magnify a line in a document, headline or tweet in an explainer
call out a detail in a press photo (badge, sign, number)
magnifier that slides along a map or chart
avoid: small Size with high Magnification shows pixels; magnify a high-res source
no border by default, so add a Stroke / ring layer or it reads as a glitch
magnifying faces of real people looks like mockery in news

params.name: Center
params.does: centre of the magnified area (pixels)

params.name: Magnification
params.does: zoom amount in percent

params.name: Size
params.does: radius / half-size of the lens in pixels

params.name: Shape
params.does: lens shape

params.name: Feather
params.does: soft edge of the lens in pixels

params.name: Link
params.does: ties size/feather to magnification

params.name: Scaling
params.does: resampling method for the enlarged pixels

params.name: Opacity
params.does: opacity of the magnified area

cards.scripting: Center is in layer pixels. Blending Mode is a 22-item popup (1 None, 2 Normal (default), 4 Add, 5 Multiply, 6 Screen ...; separators at 3, 10, 13, 18; enum_labels (read from After Effects 26.0)). Resize Layer (checkbox) lets the lens extend past layer bounds; it only works while Link is 1 None. Size is the lens radius in pixels, so Size 320 = a 640 px lens.

verified.note: The feathered lens now sits on the frame centre and shows the dark mid-frame detail enlarged over the flowers, where the old render only magnified plain grey wall into a featureless ball; detail is soft because the source is low-res and there is no ring, both already in avoid.

cards.name: Mesh Warp
cards.summary: Overlays a grid of Bezier points that are dragged by hand to bend the image. It shows nothing until the mesh is edited in the Composition panel.
use_for: bend a flat graphic onto a curved surface (pillar, flag, page curl)
subtle breathing / wobble on an illustration
fix a slightly curved horizon on a still
avoid: mesh cannot be built by script, so it is not automatable
many rows/columns with low Quality look jagged

params.name: Rows
params.does: number of mesh rows (set before editing the mesh)

params.name: Columns
params.does: number of mesh columns (set before editing the mesh)

params.name: Quality
params.does: render smoothness of the warp

params.name: Distortion Mesh
params.does: the edited grid itself (custom data)

cards.scripting: 'Distortion Mesh' is custom data and cannot be set from a spec; changing Rows/Columns resets an existing mesh. For a scripted bend use Bezier Warp, Bulge or Turbulent Displace instead.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (the mesh must be edited by hand), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Mirror
cards.summary: Splits the image along a line and reflects one side onto the other, giving a symmetric, kaleidoscope-like picture.
use_for: symmetric abstract background for a reel or title card
mirror-world look on architecture / corridor / skyline b-roll for a trailer
animated mirror-line sweep as a stylised transition (keyframe Reflection Center)
avoid: mirrored text, logos, party symbols and flags read backwards: wrong and embarrassing in political content
a mirror line through a real person's face makes a fake symmetric face: manipulated media in news
it does not extend a narrow plate (the layer size stays the same); use Motion Tile with Mirror Edges for that

params.name: Reflection Center
params.does: point the mirror line passes through (pixels)

params.name: Reflection Angle
params.does: angle of the mirror line in degrees

cards.scripting: Default centre [1920, 540] sits on the right edge, so the default shows no change; move the centre inward. Reflection Angle has no harvested limits (degrees). At 0 the line is vertical and the left side is reflected onto the right; 90 reflects the top onto the bottom; 180 keeps the right side. Verify the kept side on a frame.

verified.note: The left half is reflected onto the right around a vertical centre line, giving a symmetric twin of the left half of the frame.

cards.name: Offset
cards.summary: Slides the image inside the layer and wraps whatever leaves one edge back in on the opposite edge, like a tiled pattern.
use_for: endless scrolling texture or pattern background
check / build seamless loops
quick slip-glitch on a transition frame
scroll a ticker-like strip
avoid: on live action the wrap seam is obvious unless hidden by a glitch or motion blur

params.name: Shift Center To
params.does: where the original centre is moved to (pixels); content wraps
params.typical: animate X by the layer width for a seamless loop

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: mix back the unshifted image (raw 0-1 = 0-100%)

cards.scripting: Blend With Original is harvested as 0-1 (shown as % in the UI), so 0.5 = 50%. Default [960, 540] = no shift on a 1920x1080 layer. A shift of exactly one layer width returns to the start, good for loops.

verified.note: The image is shifted right and up with wrap-around, showing hard tile seams where the edges re-enter.

cards.name: Optics Compensation
cards.summary: Adds or removes wide-angle lens distortion: bulges the image like a fisheye, or with Reverse on, straightens barrel-distorted action-cam footage.
use_for: fisheye punch-in / whip transition on a reel hook
remove GoPro / phone wide-lens bulge (Reverse Lens Distortion on)
match graphics to a wide lens in a trailer
avoid: adding distortion (Reverse off) curves the frame edges inward and leaves transparent corners; fill them with Motion Tile (Mirror Edges) before it, or scale up
straightening (Reverse on) pushes the edges past the frame and crops them; Resize keeps them but the layer must then be scaled down
heavy fisheye on interviews distorts faces

params.name: Field Of View (FOV)
params.does: strength of the lens distortion in degrees

params.name: Reverse Lens Distortion
params.does: checkbox: remove instead of add distortion

params.name: FOV Orientation
params.does: which frame axis the FOV is measured on

params.name: View Center
params.does: optical centre of the distortion (pixels)

params.name: Resize
params.does: lets the layer grow to keep corners when reversing

params.name: Optimal Pixels (Invalidates Reversal)
params.does: checkbox: better edge pixels but result cannot be reversed exactly

cards.scripting: Checkboxes are 0/1 numbers. For a fisheye transition, keyframe FOV on an adjustment layer together with a scale ramp; add Motion Tile with Mirror Edges first so the bulged edges are not empty. Rendered check: Reverse off at FOV 90 shrinks the picture into a barrel-shaped pillow with transparent margins on all four sides (widest at the corners); the Reverse-on crop behaviour is still from memory.

verified.note: FOV 90 with Reverse off bulges the picture into a barrel-shaped pillow with transparent margins on all sides, largest at the corners.

cards.name: Polar Coordinates
cards.summary: Converts the image between rectangular and polar coordinates, curling a flat picture into a ring or 'tiny planet', or unrolling a circle into a strip.
use_for: tiny-planet look on a skyline or rally crowd for a reel opener
radial burst / tunnel background from simple stripes
circular loader or ring graphic from a straight bar
avoid: produces a visible seam where left and right edges meet unless the source is seamless
unreadable on text or faces

params.name: Interpolation
params.does: how much of the conversion is applied (raw 0-1 = 0-100%)

params.name: Type of Conversion
params.does: direction of the conversion

cards.scripting: Interpolation is harvested 0-1 although the UI shows a percentage; 1 = 100%. Default Interpolation 0 shows no change, and the default conversion is 2 Polar to Rect, so set 1 explicitly for a planet. Rect to Polar puts the TOP of the image in the centre: unflipped the sky lands in the middle (tunnel); for a tiny planet flip the source vertically first, inside a precomp or with a Transform effect above this one (the layer's own Scale is applied after effects, so it does not work). Rendered check: on a 16:9 layer the result is a circle as tall as the frame with transparent sides, so add a background or precompose into a square comp to fill the frame.

verified.note: Rect to Polar curls the photo into a round tunnel with the top of the image in the centre and the people upside-down in the lower half; the circle fits the frame height with black sides (not an oval).

cards.name: Reshape
cards.summary: Morphs the area inside one mask into the shape of another mask on the same layer, optionally limited by a boundary mask.
use_for: morph a logo or shape graphic into another outline
stretch an object to a new silhouette in a motion-graphic
avoid: needs two or three hand-drawn masks; nothing happens without them
reshaping real people's features is manipulated media in news
slow at high elasticity

params.name: Source Mask
params.does: mask outlining the area to move

params.name: Destination Mask
params.does: mask outlining the target shape

params.name: Boundary Mask
params.does: optional mask limiting the affected area

params.name: Percent
params.does: how far the morph has progressed

params.name: Elasticity
params.does: how loosely the image follows the masks (popup)

params.name: Interpolation Method
params.does: how in-between frames are computed (popup)

cards.scripting: Source/Destination/Boundary Mask are mask references and must be set by mask index after the masks exist on the layer; Correspondence Points are custom data (not scriptable from a spec). Set the three masks' mode to None so they only drive the effect and do not cut out the layer; masks must be closed. Elasticity: 1 Stiff (default), 2 Less Stiff, 3 Below Normal, 4 Normal, 5 Absolutely Normal, 6 Above Average, 7 Loose, 8 Liquid, 9 Super Fluid (looser = slower); Interpolation Method: 1 Discrete (default), 2 Linear, 3 Smooth (read from After Effects 26.0).

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs hand-drawn source and destination masks), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Ripple
cards.summary: Creates concentric water-like ripples spreading out from a centre point; the waves move on their own over time.
use_for: drop-in-water reveal on a title or logo
shockwave pulse on an impact beat in a trailer
dream / flashback wobble on a memory shot
avoid: large Wave Height on live action looks cheap and smeary
radius too small shows a hard ring edge

params.name: Radius
params.does: size of the rippled area as percent of the layer

params.name: Center of Ripple
params.does: origin of the waves (pixels)

params.name: Wave Height
params.does: strength of the distortion

params.name: Wave Width
params.does: distance between wave crests

params.name: Wave Speed
params.does: how fast the waves travel; animates on its own without keyframes (negative = inward)

params.name: Type of Conversion
params.does: wave shape

params.name: Ripple Phase
params.does: wave phase in degrees, for static or hand-timed ripples

cards.equivalent: Wave Warp (closest; Premiere has no radial ripple)
cards.scripting: Radius default 0 means no visible effect; set Radius. Wave Speed animates by itself, so a still frame at t=0 may look weaker than mid-clip. Ripple Phase has no harvested limits.

verified.note: Strong water-like wave distortion spreads over the whole frame from the centre, with scalloped top and bottom edges.
